title: Does combining a steering monitor with a steering controller create a self-defeating loop?

original_idea.body: Set up a closed probe->steer->re-read loop and measure the gap between probe-says-fixed and output-actually-fixed; one open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a monitor that gates on the very signal it perturbs is a subtle but serious design flaw (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Closed loop + independent output-safety judging requires careful experimental design (level 3).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but closed-loop + independent judging adds moving parts (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model, externally runnable architecture-safety test (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Probe + steering + inference, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Self-defeating monitor-controller feedback described as novel neglected link; mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Self-defeating monitor-controller feedback appears mostly novel.
